item.title: UN warns world is on track to double global warming unless countries change course
item.description: The United Nations warns that countries are not meeting their goals to limit warming and avoid the worst consequences of climate change.
item.content:encoded: The United Nations warns that countries are not meeting their goals to limit warming and avoid the worst consequences of climate change.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Hersher

item.title: Meet the people moving north to escape increasingly hot summers
item.description: As climate change fuels hotter summers, some Britons are moving north in search of cooler weather. Could a similar shift be on the horizon in the United States?
item.content:encoded:
As climate change fuels hotter summers, some Britons are moving north in search of cooler weather. Could a similar shift be on the horizon in the United States?

(Image credit: Dan Kitwood)

item.title: United Nations report highlights significant increase in U.S. climate pollution
item.description: The U.S. is the only major economy where planet-warming pollution dramatically increased last year. The United Nations warns the planet is on track for catastrophic warming.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. is the only major economy where planet-warming pollution dramatically increased last year. The United Nations warns the planet is on track for catastrophic warming.

(Image credit: Charlie Riedel)

item.title: A Kelvin wave raised sea levels on the West Coast. More are coming
item.description: A large underwater wave moved up the West Coast, raising sea levels. Scientists say it's driven by El Niño and it's going to happen again.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Some of the most pristine coral reefs have a secret weapon: birds
item.description: Coral reefs are facing increasing threats around the globe. But on a remote Pacific island, scientists have found that reefs can get help from a surprising ally: seabirds.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Isaias pummels the Gulf Coast, and plows through Alabama
item.description: Hurricane Isaias landed Friday night on the Florida Gulf Coast. The storm was expected to bring life-threatening storm surge, damaging winds, flooding and the possibility of tornados.

item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep talks with former NOAA official Carolyn Gruber about vulnerabilities in the infrastructure of coastal cities during extreme weather events.
